The ISS (ZARYA) should perform the avoidance burn because it is the only craft able to maneuver and its post-burn collision probability (2.3 × 10⁻⁸) falls well below the action threshold of 1 × 10⁻⁵, whereas the debris cannot move. The burn yields a resulting miss distance of about 4 200 m and a probability of roughly 0.000000023. Fuel-reserve (70 %) and mission-impact (80 %) values are assumed inputs, and a human flight director must approve the maneuver.
